findings.trigger: A group of three members, 'start' pressed. On an attempt, cog.get_status(...) for member C returns success=False (Docker error, container momentarily unreadable) while A and B are up. Line 122 `continue` drops C from `running`, so `running == [True, True]` and `_has_taken_effect('start', running)` returns True at line 132: the wait reports 'the action showed' for the whole group although one member was never confirmed. Same for 'stop': two members stopped, the third unreadable -> `not any([False, False])` -> True. The docstring at 69-72 says this is exactly the 'acts on fewer and reports done' the function exists to prevent; the caller then draws the panel without the 'Not confirmed yet' embed.
findings.suggestion: Treat an unreadable member as 'not confirmed for this attempt': track a `complete = True` flag, set it False when a status read fails, and only `return True` when `complete and _has_taken_effect(...)`. (Alternatively append a sentinel and make _has_taken_effect require len(running) == len(targets).) Keep the ladder running so a transient read error does not end the wait early.

findings.trigger: AdminOverviewView(timeout=None) is registered with bot.add_view so old overview messages keep answering (docstring 182-186). A click on an old message is then dispatched to the REGISTERED button object, whose `disabled` is whatever `has_running_containers` the registration passed - not the state of the button on the message. Discord never delivers a click on a disabled button, so the branch `if self.disabled` (401, and 488 in Stop All) can only ever fire when the two disagree: registered with False while containers are running -> the admin presses Restart All / Stop All on an existing overview after a bot restart and is told '❌ No running containers to restart/stop' although containers run. If the registration passes True, the branch is dead code. Either way it never protects anything.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `self.disabled` short-circuit (the shared loop already skips non-running containers and reports 'Skipped (not running)'), or decide from the current status cache instead of the button object's attribute.
findings.unsure_why: The bot.add_view call and the value it passes for has_running_containers are outside this section, and I cannot tell whether py-cord refreshes the registered item's `disabled` from the message components before dispatching the callback.

findings.trigger: Group G is active and its allowed_actions contain 'restart'; member C's own container configuration has allowed_actions ['start'] only. An admin picks G in the stack menu and confirms. _servers_of replaces every member's allowed_actions with the GROUP's (175-176), so the shared loop (admin_overview.py:80) sees 'restart' allowed and restarts C. The same admin pressing 'Restart All' on the same overview a minute earlier had C skipped as 'action not allowed'. Z5 as written in SPEC.md demands 'the container allows the action' on every path; the code cites an operator decision of 2026-09-24 that SPEC.md does not record, and the B2 refinement in SPEC.md says explicitly 'which actions are allowed stays with the container's own allowed_actions'.
findings.suggestion: Either record the 2026-09-24 group decision in SPEC.md as a deliberate exception to Z5 (so the next review does not report it again and the two bulk paths' different answers for the same container are documented), or keep the container's own allowed_actions and let the group's list only add the group-level lock at line 157.
findings.unsure_why: The code comments state this is the operator's deliberate decision; SPEC.md (which is what I am told to judge against) does not contain it and its B2 wording points the other way. I cannot tell whether SPEC.md is simply behind.

findings.trigger: In ConfirmRestartStackButton.callback anything raised between the lock and the loop - `from services.docker_service.docker_action_service import ...` failing with ImportError (the two sibling confirm buttons handle exactly this at admin_overview.py:770-778), `controllable()` or the group service raising something other than OSError - propagates out of the callback. The `finally` releases the lock, but the interaction was deferred and no followup is sent: the admin sees a spinner that ends in nothing, with only a log line.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the body like the two sibling confirm buttons do (catch the service errors, send '❌ An error occurred during the restart operation.' as an ephemeral followup) so the three bulk buttons fail the same way.
findings.unsure_why: Which exception types _servers_of/controllable/the group service can raise is outside this section; if all of them only raise OSError (caught inside _servers_of) the gap is narrower than described.

findings.trigger: An assigned admin restarts a group of 30 containers of which 25 are not assigned to them. `not_touched` has 25 names; line 310 prints `not_touched[:20]` with no '... and 5 more', so five containers that were not restarted are missing from a list headed 'Not touched'. The same line gives the reason as 'not in DDC, or switched off', which is wrong for the assigned-admin case (they are in DDC and on) and contradicts the docstring at 127-131 that switched-off members ARE restarted through their group.
findings.suggestion: Use fit_lines(...) with a 'more' callback as StackSelect.callback already does for the member list, and split the reason: 'not in DDC' for `missing`, 'not assigned to you' for the members controllable() removed.

findings.trigger: An admin with `admin_containers: {"<id>": ["valheim"]}` presses Stop All (or Restart All) while valheim is inactive. After controllable() the list is empty and the message is '❌ No active servers configured.' - but servers ARE configured and active; the real reason is that none of them are assigned to this admin. stack_restart.py:297 has the same shape: '**{stack}** has no active containers any more' when the group is full of active containers that are merely not assigned to the presser.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish the two empties: if `servers` was non-empty before controllable() and empty after, say 'None of the active containers is assigned to you.'

findings.trigger: A server entry whose `allowed_actions` key exists with the value null/None (`server.get('allowed_actions', [])` returns None, the default is not applied). `verb not in None` raises TypeError inside the bulk loop, after earlier containers were already restarted/stopped. TypeError is not in any except tuple of _act_on_running_servers (123-128) or the confirm callbacks (793, 953); the lock is released by `finally`, but the admin gets no summary at all for a bulk action that was half done.
findings.suggestion: `verb not in (server.get('allowed_actions') or [])`, and count the entry as not_allowed.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the config service can ever hand out an entry with allowed_actions = None is outside this section; if it always normalises to a list the trigger cannot occur.

findings.trigger: The operator stops container X by hand (docker CLI / Unraid UI). Before the status cache has been refreshed, an admin confirms Restart All. Line 88-101 takes is_running from the cached entry without looking at its age, X counts as running, `docker restart` on a stopped container STARTS it, and the summary says 'Successfully restarted' one more than expected. The confirmation text promised to restart 'ALL running containers'; a container that was deliberately stopped comes back up.
findings.suggestion: Either check the cache entry's timestamp against the refresh interval and count a stale entry as 'unknown' (already reported as 'Not checked'), or ask the daemon for the current state before a bulk action - it is one call per container and the loop already paces itself.
findings.unsure_why: The status cache refresh interval and whether the cache is invalidated on external state changes are outside this section; with a short interval the window is a few seconds.

findings.trigger: answer_or_post exists so the bulk summary is not lost when the followup cannot be sent. It catches only discord.errors.NotFound/HTTPException. A transport failure while sending the ephemeral followup (connection reset, DNS hiccup - aiohttp's ClientOSError is an OSError, not an HTTPException) is not caught here, so the channel fallback at 153-160 never runs, and in the callers the OSError is not in the except tuples either (admin_overview 793/953 catch RuntimeError but not OSError; stack_restart 318 has only a finally). The summary of a completed Restart All / Stop All is lost entirely and the admin sees nothing, which is the case the function was written for.
findings.suggestion: Catch `(discord.errors.DiscordException, RuntimeError, OSError)` around the followup (the same tuple the channel fallback already uses at 160), so every failure to reach the presser falls through to the channel post.
findings.unsure_why: I am relying on memory of the aiohttp/discord exception hierarchy (ClientOSError -> OSError, not wrapped into HTTPException by discord.py's request loop); I could not verify it here.

findings.trigger: current_targets renames a group that shares a name with a Compose project to `_("{name} (group)")` (114). _servers_of recovers the group name by stripping `_("{name} (group)").format(name="")` as a SUFFIX (145-147). In a locale whose translation puts the name last (e.g. '(Gruppe) {name}') the suffix does not match, `plain` stays the whole menu label, members_of() does not find the group, `group` stays None, and the restart falls through to `current_targets().get(name)` - which does return the group's containers, but now with the CONTAINERS' allowed_actions and without the second lock at 157. The same press behaves differently per language.
findings.suggestion: Carry the plain group name in the menu's value/self.stacks (the option value is already an index, so a (label, kind, plain_name) tuple costs nothing) instead of reconstructing it from the translated label.
findings.unsure_why: The 40 locale files are outside this section; if every translation keeps {name} first the trigger cannot occur today, but nothing pins that down.

notes:
Findings without their own verdict slot (one verdict per name): F4 and F5 also belong to cogs/stack_restart.py:272 ConfirmRestartStackButton.callback (F3 was attached); F6 and F7 also belong to cogs/admin_overview.py:692 ConfirmRestartAllButton.callback (F8 was attached); F7 applies to ConfirmStopAllButton.callback as well.

Observed but no trigger I can state from this section alone:
(1) AdminOverviewAdminButton.callback (266) checks nothing at all - neither the channel permission nor the admin list - and builds the dropdown from ALL controllable_entries(all_servers), while SPEC B2 says the ephemeral dropdown offers only the assigned containers. The comment at 283-284 claims 'in control channels all users have access', but the B2 comments in the same file say the overview is also used where the channel permits nothing. All of this must be enforced inside AdminContainerSelectView (user_id is passed), which I cannot see. If it is not, anybody who can see a status channel opens a working admin panel.
(2) The same summary text exists twice: _restart_summary (163-174) and the inline copy in ConfirmStopAllButton.callback (933-941). Identical today; the file's own history (54-56) shows what happens to such copies.
(3) Two contradictory beliefs about get_all_servers(): admin_overview 752-755 filters `active` as if inactive entries were present; stack_restart 170-171 says get_all_servers() leaves them out. If the latter is right, the documented wish that a switched-off member is still restarted through its group depends on the status cache holding a 'running' entry for an inactive container; if the cache is only filled for active ones, such a member lands in 'Not checked (no current status)' and is not restarted - honestly reported, but not what the operator asked for.
(4) control_helpers._channel_has_permission (127): a channel whose entry is an empty dict `{}` falls back to default_channel_permissions rather than to 'nothing'. Whether the panel can write such an entry is not visible here. Not in the plan (private name).
(5) control_helpers.container_select (98-103): if get_cached_servers() returns None the comprehension raises TypeError; the code only warns. It also logs the full container list at INFO on every autocomplete keystroke.
(6) control_helpers.refused_while_busy (343-344) subtracts running['timestamp'] from an aware datetime; a naive timestamp written by ActionButton would raise TypeError inside the press. The writer is outside this section.
(7) validate_custom_address refuses every IPv6 address (':' is split as a port separator); this was already so before the D28 change, not a regression.
(8) _act_on_running_servers: after the 30 s wait_for timeout the container is counted 'Failed' although the dispatched docker call may still complete - conservative direction (B6, no resend), not a finding.
(9) _delayed_overview_update (807-813, 967-973) catches only RuntimeError; anything else from cog._update_overview_message ends as 'Task exception was never retrieved'. The overview is redrawn periodically anyway, so only cosmetic.
(10) The three bulk buttons deliberately check the admin list and not the channel (B2, read as instructed, not reported).
